decision.title: The book's code-generation project (packet book-3)
decision.summary: The book gains Chapter 12, a project that generates a TypeScript client, Node.js handler and OpenAPI document from an XSD schema and an API description, with the generated files checked in sync.

body.p: , after and . The owner asked for a chapter on using XQuery, XSD and XSLT for code generation, such as RPC between the browser and the backend in the manner of SvelteKit's remote functions.

item.p: Place. A new top-level Chapter 12, "Project: Generating Code from a Schema", after Performance and before the appendices, so the numbers of Chapters 1 to 11 (cited elsewhere in the book) hold. Four sections: codegen.md (the sources and their validation), codegen-typescript.md, codegen-running.md, codegen-pipeline.md; examples in docs/book/examples/codegen. One sentence links to it from the XQuery, XSLT and XSD parts and the introduction; the book's glossary gains "Remote function" and "String constructor".

The example. library.xsd (simple types with pattern, maxLength, enumeration and range facets; complex types read as JSON objects: minOccurs="0" is optional, maxOccurs="unbounded" an array) and api.xml (queries and commands), checked by api.xsd with sxml validate. typescript.xqm writes TypeScript with string constructors (types and checks, a fetch client, a Node.js handler) over a hand-written runtime.ts; generate.xq stores the files with fn:put and the text method; openapi.xsl writes OpenAPI 3.1 with template rules and xsl:map. Unknown facets and unknown type names are errors of the generators, not silently dropped. The generated files are kept in generated/, and the book's diff -r against a fresh run is the "in sync" check, so the book check also keeps them current: regenerate them (sh generate.sh in that directory) when the generator, the schema or the CLI's output changes.

Running the code. codegen-running.md runs node demo.ts (Node.js 22.18 or later strips the types; the generated code uses only erasable syntax). It is marked <!-- requires: javascript -->, so the check runs it only with SXML_JAVASCRIPT set, where Node.js is known to be present; the package link it makes is unused.
Finding for later (QUEUE, not fixed here): a syntax error inside an enclosed expression of a string constructor (`{ ... }`) is reported at line 1, column 1 of the module instead of its own place.

Verified: tools/check-book-examples.sh on a release build of a HEAD snapshot with SXML_JAVASCRIPT set: all 30 examples of the four files match; mdbook build succeeds; the generated TypeScript type-checks with tsc --strict.
